Topics · Hard times

I am afraid of dying. Does the Quran ease that?

Sleep is likened to death, the soul at rest invited back, and mercy covers all. No detail of what follows.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 3

﴿ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَٱلَّتِى لَمْ تَمُتْ فِى مَنَامِهَا ۖ فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:42

Translation

If he set his heart on himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath, all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.

Original · Hebrew

אִם־יָשִׂ֣ים אֵלָ֣יו לִבּ֑וֹ רוּח֥וֹ וְ֝נִשְׁמָת֗וֹ אֵלָ֥יו יֶאֱסֹֽף׃ יִגְוַ֣ע כָּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר יָ֑חַד וְ֝אָדָ֗ם עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָשֽׁוּב׃

Job · 34:14-15

World English Bible

Every night we do something strange: we lie down, let go of awareness, and trust we will wake. The verse puts sleep and death in one sentence: God takes souls at their death, and those that have not died in their sleep, then keeps those whose death He decreed and sends the others back for a set term. You hand yourself over every night to the One who keeps and sends. Perhaps this nightly trust has something to say to the fear of death.

A question for you

What frightens you most about death?

If you sayThe unknown.
ThenThat is the most honest fear. This page does not claim to describe the unknown in detail; it says what is in the verses.
If you sayLeaving those I love.
ThenThat is love's fear. The next step has a call to the settled soul.
If you sayPain at the end.
ThenThat is a fair fear. This page says nothing about medicine; you may ask your doctors and loved ones about care.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ٢٧ ٱرْجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً٢٨ فَٱدْخُلِى فِى عِبَـٰدِى٢٩ وَٱدْخُلِى جَنَّتِى٣٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

[To the righteous it will be said], "O reassured soul, Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him], And enter among My [righteous] servants And enter My Paradise."

Quran · Al-Fajr 89:27-30

Translation

and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

Original · Hebrew

וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ׃

Ecclesiastes · 12:7

World English Bible

The Quran addresses the soul at rest: return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, enter among My servants, enter My garden. It is a call of invitation, not a frightening command. The word 'return' means going back to a place you came from. The word 'at rest' means a soul that has found its calm. So the call names the end of the road a return, and what follows a joining with God's servants. There is no threat in this sentence.

A question for you

How does the sound of this call strike you?

If you sayReassuring.
ThenThat is what the text intends: a call that is near, not frightening.
If you sayFar from me.
ThenYou may feel it is not for you. The last page here speaks of the breadth of mercy.
If you sayI do not know.
ThenThat is fine. You are not asked to know now.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَٱكْتُبْ لَنَا فِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ۚ قَالَ عَذَابِىٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنْ أَشَآءُ ۖ وَرَحْمَتِى وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ ۚ فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and [also] in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You." [Allāh] said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things." So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakāh and those who believe in Our verses-

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:156

Translation

Yahweh is good to all. His tender mercies are over all his works.

Original · Hebrew

טוֹב־יְהוָ֥ה לַכֹּ֑ל וְ֝רַחֲמָ֗יו עַל־כָּל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃

the Psalms · 145:9

World English Bible

In the verse God says: My mercy encompasses all things. The simplest thing in it is that mercy is not confined to any one thing or person; it takes in all things. The verse goes on to say for whom this mercy is written, so read it to the end. But its first sentence is enough to begin with: what a person fears in death lies inside what mercy encompasses.

A question for you

What do you take from this page?

If you sayThat I may fear without being blamed.
ThenFear is allowed here. No one asks you not to be afraid.
If you sayTo read the verse in full.
ThenA good idea. Read it quietly, without hurry.
If you sayTo talk to someone about this.
ThenThat is among the best things to do. There is also a page on what happens after death.

The same in the other books

But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.

וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לִשְׁמֹ֗עַ וְלֹא־זָכְר֤וּ נִפְלְאֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּהֶ֔ם וַיַּקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־עָרְפָּ֔ם וַיִּתְּנוּ־רֹ֛אשׁ לָשׁ֥וּב לְעַבְדֻתָ֖ם בְּמִרְיָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֩ אֱל֨וֹהַּ סְלִיח֜וֹת חַנּ֧וּן וְרַח֛וּם אֶֽרֶךְ־אַפַּ֥יִם וְרַב־חֶ֖סֶד וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּֽם׃

Nehemiah · 9:17

World English Bible

Translation

Yahweh is gracious and righteous. Yes, our God is merciful. Yahweh preserves the simple. I was brought low, and he saved me. Return to your rest, my soul, for Yahweh has dealt bountifully with you. For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling. I will walk before Yahweh in the land of the living.

Original · Hebrew

חַנּ֣וּן יְהֹוָ֣ה וְצַדִּ֑יק וֵ֖אלֹהֵ֣ינוּ מְרַחֵֽם׃ שֹׁמֵ֣ר פְּתָאיִ֣ם יְהֹוָ֑ה דַּ֝לּוֹתִ֗י וְלִ֣י יְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃ שׁוּבִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָ֑יְכִי כִּֽי־יְ֝הוָ֗ה גָּמַ֥ל עָלָֽיְכִי׃ כִּ֤י חִלַּ֥צְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֗י מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת־עֵינִ֥י מִן־דִּמְעָ֑ה אֶת־רַגְלִ֥י מִדֶּֽחִי׃ אֶ֭תְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּ֝אַרְצ֗וֹת הַֽחַיִּֽים׃
